items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law and the state finance law, in relation to the housing opportunities for people to empower excellence and equity trust fund
items.lawCode: Add §41.56, Ment Hyg L; add §99-aa, St Fin L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S872

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the mental hygiene law and the state finance law, in
relation to the housing opportunities for people to empower excellence
and equity trust fund

 PURPOSE GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To support aging family caregivers who provide for those with
developmental disabilities who can no longer effectively provide care
due to their own age related disabilities

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 establishes legislative findings.

Section 2 amends the mental hygiene law by adding a new section 41.56.

(a) The HOPE trust fund is established for the purpose of providing
access to rental housing for persons with developmental disabilities
as well as facilitating new construction and renovation. The fund
would be administered by the Office of People with Developmental
Disabilities in consultation with the Department of Health. OPWDD and
DOH would provide a mechanism to identify and prioritize need by
region and would work with other agencies and interested persons in
planning for satisfaction of identified needs.

(b) Funding for the trust fund would be used for housing and other
non-Medicaid funded supports to insure identified priorities can be
met, in consultation with the Commissioner of Health. The Commissioner
of OPWDD would allocate the funds by region each year.

(c) An annual plan for the use of the HOPE Trust Fund would be
developed and approved by the HOPE Trust Fund Board, which would be
composed of the Commissioner of OPWDD (chair), and twelve members of
the public appointed by the Governor. There would be two
recommendations from the Speaker of the Assembly, two from the
Temporary President of the Senate, one from the Minority Leader of the
Assembly, and one from the Minority Leader of the Senate. The
Commissioners of Health and Housing and Community Renewal, the
Director of the Division of the Budget and the Chief Executive
Officers of the Dormitory Authority and Mortgage Agency would serve as
ex officio members of the board. Membership of the board would include
self-advocates, parents, guardians, and family members of persons with
developmental disabilities and others with expertise in the provision
of residential services.

(d) In developing a plan for the disbursement of funds from the HOPE
Trust Fund, the board would:

(i) Determine eligibility requirements for individuals with
developmental disabilities.

(ii) Establish audit protocols for non-profit organizations licensed.

(iii) Prepare an annual progress report on the status of persons
waiting for services, the number of those serviced through the fund,
the settings such persons are served in and the extent of federal
financial participation.

(e) In order to receive HOPE Fund monies, an authorized provider of
waiver services must contract with OPWDD and agree to terms and
conditions, which would include:

(i) A description of how operating expenses of the project shall be
met.

(ii) A description of the services and supports which would be
available to persons served.

(iii) A description of how the project will provide services to
eligible individuals.

(iv) Type of facility proposed.

(v) Other terms and conditions that may be required by such office.

(f) The board may authorize expenditures from the fund for expenses
deemed appropriate to develop person centered residential services:

(i) Technical assistance for general project development.

(ii) Necessary legal, architectural, financial, and other consulting
services.

(iii) Cost of renovation, construction, and rehabilitation for
residential projects authorized.

(iv) Funding for rental assistance and housing subsidies.

(g) OPWDD is directed to authorize and fund any necessary home and
community based Medicaid waiver services for individuals placed into
projects completed.

Section 3 amends the state finance law by adding a new section 99-y.

(1) The HOPE Trust Fund is established in joint custody of the State
Comptroller and Commissioner of Taxation and Finance. (2) The fund
will consist of all monies appropriated for its purpose, all monies
required by this section to be paid into or credited to the fund, and
no less than five hundred million dollars collected by the state in
settlements from banking institutions or other financial services
organizations. Grants, gifts, or bequests can be accepted to the fund.
(3) Monies of the fund, when allocated, will be available for
administrative costs of the HOPE Trust Fund Board and for funding the
costs of providing housing and residential supports to persons with
developmental disabilities.

(4) Monies will be payable from the fund on the audit and warrant of
the State Comptroller on vouchers approved and certified by the
Commissioner of OPWDD.

Section 4, immediate effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Adults with intellectual or developmental disabilities have lived at
home with family their entire lives, which has resulted in substantial
savings for New York State. As these family caregivers age, however,
they no longer can provide care due to their own age related
disabilities. It is incumbent upon the state of New York that a source
of funding is provided in order to allow these families access to
appropriate residential opportunities.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

S. 6840 of 2016; Referred to Mental Health and Developmental
Disabilities

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :
To be determined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

summary: Establishes the housing opportunities for people to empower excellence and equity (HOPE) trust fund to provide access to rental housing; to facilitate the construction, renovation and rehabilitation of facilities to provide additional residential opportunities; to develop new and innovative approaches to residential living and to promote creation of sustainable living environments for people with developmental disabilities.
